decision: InvoiceDate -> datetime; CustomerID float -> text ID; ID/code columns read as text
business_impact: IDs are labels (never used as numeric features); dates enable time analysis

decision: Added Year, Month, DayOfWeek, DayOfWeekNum, Hour, YearMonth
business_impact: Enables seasonality, weekday and hourly analysis. Note: Dec 2011 is incomplete (data ends on the 9th)

decision: Kept in df and flagged (HasCustomerID). Used for sales/product/time/country EDA; excluded from RFM and clustering
business_impact: Revenue totals stay complete; customer-level analysis only uses identifiable customers

decision: Flagged (neg qty, non-C invoice, price 0, no ID); excluded from revenue and customer analysis
business_impact: Not customer sales or returns; keeping them would distort revenue and basket sizes

decision: Flagged (price 0, not an adjustment); excluded from revenue and RFM
business_impact: Free items add no revenue but would inflate order counts and quantities

decision: Kept in df (negative revenue nets out automatically); flagged IsCancellation + MatchStatus (matched / partial / no original / no CustomerID)
business_impact: Net revenue is correct; return analysis can separate verified returns from unmatched ones (14.7% unmatched, may refer to pre-2010-12 purchases)

decision: Flagged IsNonProduct (postage, fees, manual, discount, samples); excluded from product and basket analysis
business_impact: Fees and postage are not products; keeping them would pollute top-product rankings and basket sizes

decision: Kept as normal sales: gift_0001_* vouchers, DCGS party bags/ashtray, PADS (near-zero price) reviewed individually
business_impact: Small volume (about 40 rows); real revenue, so kept; vouchers are not physical demand, noted as a limitation

decision: Dropped rows identical in all 8 original columns (kept first copy)
business_impact: Removes ~0.2% of revenue; prevents double-counted units and inflated basket sizes. Caveat: a genuine repeated scan of the same item would also be removed

decision: Flagged cancellation lines that reverse an identical purchase within 60 min (IsQuickReversal); kept in df
business_impact: Net revenue unchanged, but return metrics are reported with and without them. Two orders (~80k units each) make up ~52% of returned value

decision: R and M scored with pd.qcut (5 quantiles). F scored with fixed bins [1, 2, 3-4, 5-8, 9+] because qcut cannot split F: about a third of customers have exactly 1 order
business_impact: F groups are not equal-sized (see 9.2), but the score keeps its direction: higher F = more orders

decision: Clustering on raw Recency, Frequency, Monetary -> log1p -> StandardScaler (not on 1-5 scores, not on CustomerID)
business_impact: Prevents wholesale whales from dominating distances; keeps within-score differences that quantile scores erase

decision: K-Means K=5 on all 4,333 customers was explored first; it was later superseded (see Final segmentation)
business_impact: Without isolating the whales, one cluster mixed trade accounts with regular loyal buyers; the K=5 result was not stable once whales were set aside

decision: Whales (DBSCAN outlier AND spend >= P95, 39 customers) + K-Means K=4 on the rest, named from segment statistics
business_impact: K=5 became unstable without the whales (min ARI 0.415); K=4 has the best silhouette (0.337) and every segment >= 17% of customers

decision: 'Fading Regulars' renamed 'Due-Now Regulars': their median recency (56 d) equals their usual order gap (58.5 d)
business_impact: Avoids a misleading 'fading' label; the action is a timely reorder reminder, not a heavy win-back offer
